answer_1.quote: automatically generating distractors is substantially less researched ... we attempt using machine learning (ML) to aid teachers in creating distractors for reading comprehension MCQs.
answer_1.outputs: distractors (wrong but plausible options) for multiple-choice questions

answer_2.quote: Automatic evaluation metrics, such as BLEU, ROUGE, METEOR, CIDEr, became popular in NLG in recent years. ... we have experimented with a number of quantitative metrics and propose the following set to be used ...

answer_4.quote: We have used distractors generated on the test set by the best u-PMLM model ... to conduct human evaluation in 2 stages: from a perspective of a student and a teacher.
answer_4.guideline: For the student evaluation: subjects were instructed to choose the most plausible answer without reading the original texts. For the teacher evaluation: teachers were instructed to select those of generated distractors (if any) deemed suitable for testing reading comprehension and to provide reasons for rejection.
